title: README's Homebrew section says the tap does not exist, and its short-name install is refused by Homebrew 7.0.10
body:
Found from Molt on 2026-10-20 (Molt ST0005), while checking which install docs a Homebrew 7.0.10 user could follow. The "Or install it with Homebrew, on macOS or Linux" section of `README.md` is stale in two ways.

1. It opens "**The tap does not exist yet.** Whether it is created, and whether it is public, has not been decided". Issue 0195 closed that. The tap is `matthewsinclair/homebrew-devbin`, private on GitHub, tapped on rhadamanth from `ssh://git@github.com/matthewsinclair/homebrew-devbin.git`, and `brew info matthewsinclair/devbin/devbin` reports stable 0.1.12, installed on request.

2. Its install line is the short name, `brew install devbin`, after the `brew tap`. Homebrew 7.0.10 refuses a short name from a tap it does not trust. This was measured on rhadamanth with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` pointed at an empty trust store, for another third-party tap:
   - `brew install --dry-run babashka` exits 1 with "Error: Refusing to load formula borkdude/brew/babashka from untrusted tap borkdude/brew. Run `brew trust --formula borkdude/brew/babashka` or `brew trust borkdude/brew` to trust it."
   - The full name, `brew install --dry-run borkdude/brew/babashka`, prints "==> Trusted formula borkdude/brew/babashka" and exits 0.

   kovacs-sysadm hit the same refusal the same day, installing Utilz by its short name on kovacs. devbin's own formula was not probed this way, but the gate is Homebrew's, not the formula's.

Fix: write the install as `brew install matthewsinclair/devbin/devbin`, keeping the `brew tap` with the ssh URL, which a private tap still needs. Replace the "does not exist yet" paragraph with what is true now. Intent's README already installs by full name (`brew install matthewsinclair/intent/intent`).

## Resolution

Fixed at 1e29275b in the 0.1.13 batch, on landing suite 20261023-2029 at 23f5f70e (2435 of 2435 ok, 5 skips, seal empty) (dc built it in a scratch clone of main at 667b7a8b; vc landed it).

- The README's "Or install it with Homebrew" section says what is true now: the tap is `matthewsinclair/homebrew-devbin`, private while devbin's repository is, as `docs/releasing.md` says. Both repositories read PRIVATE with `gh repo view` on 2026-10-23. The "does not exist yet" paragraph is gone.
- Its install line is the formula's full name, `brew install matthewsinclair/devbin/devbin`, after the same `brew tap` with the ssh url.
- No other doc installs devbin by its short name. The short-name `brew upgrade devbin` in the runtime's remedy, its pages, the formula's caveats and the README stays, because each reaches only a machine where the formula is installed, and so trusted.
- devbin's own formula, probed on rhadamanth under Homebrew 7.0.10-69-g4321e3d with an empty trust store, dry runs only: `brew install --dry-run devbin` exits 1 with "Refusing to load formula matthewsinclair/devbin/devbin from untrusted tap matthewsinclair/devbin."; the full name prints "Trusted formula matthewsinclair/devbin/devbin", exits 0 and records the formula in the store; after it, `brew upgrade --dry-run devbin` loads and exits 0.
- `tests/unit/documentation.bats` holds it: no doc a user reads carries a short-name install line, and the README carries the full-name one. It is red on main (`README.md:241:brew install devbin`) and green at the fix, under BSD and GNU tools, and declares what its pattern cannot catch.
